 Election Day 2026: Live updates
 Updates from around the state as Virginians select their next slate of congressional representatives and votes on three constitutional amendments.

 Polls are open, Virginia 
 Constitutional amendments would ensure Virginia is ‘a safe place,’ Stafford voter says
 By Nathaniel Cline - Tuesday November 3, 2026 12:15 pm 
 A view from inside a voting precinct in Stafford County on Nov. 3, 2026. The polling place is in Virginia’s 7th Congressional District. (Photo by Nathaniel Cline/Virginia Mercury) 
 Stafford County voters at Hartwood Elementary School recorded the highest in-person turnout four years ago, with over 2,015 voters. By late morning on Tuesday, the polling place was on track to reach that milestone again. 
 As of 11:45 a.m., the precinct was averaging about 120 voters an hour. 
 A total of 851 voters had checked in, representing 16% of the 5,000 voters registered in the Hartwood Precinct. 
 As in previous years, voters are deciding the winner of the 7th Congressional District race . Democratic incumbent Eugene Vindman faces Republican Douglas Ollivant, and Libertarian Taner Lopez. Independents  Alaha Ahrar, Randall Terry and Joshua Ertle are also on the ballot. 
 Charles Lawrence, a Stafford County voter, said voting was important for him today because he wanted to do his part to keep Republicans in control. 
 “I just want the Republicans to win because I don’t want everything to be overturned over what was done the last two years,” said Lawrence. “I want things to keep going the way they’re going and I would like to get the (Iran) war over also, so hopefully they will.” 
 Stafford voter Kenya Bell said casting her ballot on the constitutional amendments to protect reproductive rights, marriage equality and voting restoration for former felons was a priority for her. 
 Without the choice to approve the amendments, she said would’ve had to move out of the commonwealth. 
 “There was too much on the line,” Bell said. “In this current environment and this current culture, (opponents) are looking to strip away and gut out all of our rights federally. So I needed to make sure that Virginia was going to be a safe place to continue to reside.” 
 Some voters cited  critical concerns including  mounting economic pressures, federal employment shifts, a lack of affordable housing, and infrastructure needs. 
 The 7th District seat is one of the most competitive in Virginia. 
 Jones urges Virginians to vote, thanks election workers
 By Markus Schmidt - 10:01 am 
 Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones in Hampton, Va., August 2026.  (Photo by Charlotte Rene Woods/Virginia Mercury) 
 Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones encouraged eligible voters to cast their ballots Tuesday and thanked election officials for their work as polls opened across the state.
 “Our ability to choose our leaders with free, fair, and safe elections is what makes our republic special,” Jones said in an Election Day statement.
 Jones urged Virginians who had not yet voted to visit their polling place or return their absentee ballot.
 “I also want to thank the dedicated election officials who are working long hours today and will be working well into the early morning hours in support of our democratic process,” he said.
 Last updated: 10:01 am
 DOJ lists four Virginia jurisdictions for Election Day monitoring
 By Markus Schmidt - 9:20 am 
 The U.S. Department of Justice plans to send election monitors or observers to Charlottesville, Fairfax, Prince William and Virginia Beach on Tuesday as part of what it calls its largest election monitoring effort.
 The department announced approximately 1,000 monitors and observers nationwide, with deployments in all 50 states for the first time. The release did not specify polling locations or how many personnel would be assigned to Virginia.
 Coordinated by the department’s Civil Rights Division, the effort will check compliance with federal voting rights laws, including protections against voter intimidation and discrimination and requirements ensuring access for voters with disabilities.
 “I am very proud we are deploying the largest monitoring effort in DOJ history, and pursuing transparency for elections in an assertive and nondiscriminatory manner,” Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon said in the announcement.
 Virginia Elections Commissioner Steve Koski, appointed by Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger, told The Mercury in a recent interview that state and local officials had prepared for potential disruptions.
 “I cannot speak for any potential actions that anybody else would take. But regardless, I feel prepared, I feel our localities are prepared to run this election well, and we will do so in accordance with the law,” he said.
 Voters can report concerns about federal voting rights violations to the department at 1-800-253-3931 , by email at [email protected] or through its civil rights complaint portal .
 Last updated: 9:21 am
 Spanberger urges Virginians to vote, citing ‘chaos out of Washington’
 By Markus Schmidt - 8:25 am 
 Gov. Abigail Spanberger speaks to reporters in Richmond, July 2026. (Photo by Markus Schmidt/Virginia Mercury) 
 Gov. Abigail Spanberger urged eligible Virginians to vote Tuesday, pointing to congressional races and three proposed constitutional amendments as opportunities to shape the state’s and country’s future.
 “Virginians can use their votes to choose representatives who they believe will address their top-of-mind challenges, contend with the chaos out of Washington, and always put them first,” Spanberger said in an Election Day statement.
 The Democratic governor also highlighted amendments addressing reproductive rights, marriage equality and voting rights.
 “At a time when chaos and uncertainty continue to dominate our national politics, we can send a clear message about the future we want to build — one grounded in accountability, steady leadership, and a commitment to delivering for people.”
 Last updated: 8:47 am
 Polls are open, Virginia
 By Staff Report - 8:23 am 
 Virginians will vote Tuesday in the 2026 midterm elections, with control of Congress and three proposed constitutional amendments at stake after a record early voting turnout.
 Polls are open statewide from 6 a.m. until 7 p.m., giving voters their final opportunity to weigh in on races for the U.S. Senate and all 11 of Virginia’s U.S. House seats, along with proposed protections for reproductive rights, marriage equality and voting rights.
 Read this to get prepared before you vote, and check out our voter guide if you need to learn more about the candidates, races and amendments on the ballot.
 We’ll be posting updates from around the state all day; check back here soon.

 const now = new Date();
 document
 .querySelectorAll('.timeSinceNav time, .timeSince time')
 .forEach((timeEl) => {
 const postDate = new Date(timeEl.getAttribute('datetime'));
 timeEl.innerText = getRelativeTime(now, postDate);
 });
 });
 const getRelativeTime = (current, target) => {
 const timeDiff = Math.floor((target - current) / 1000);
 const relativeTime = new Intl.RelativeTimeFormat('en', {
 numeric: 'always',
 });
 if (Math.abs(timeDiff) < 60) { // Within minute
 return relativeTime.format(Math.min(Math.round(timeDiff), 1), 'second');
 } else if (Math.abs(timeDiff) < 60 * 60) { // Within hour
 return relativeTime.format(Math.round(timeDiff / 60), 'minute');
 } else if (Math.abs(timeDiff) < 60 * 60 * 24) { // Within day
 return relativeTime.format(Math.round(timeDiff / (60 * 60)), 'hour');
 } else if (Math.abs(timeDiff) < 60 * 60 * 24 * 7) { // Within week
 return relativeTime.format(Math.round(timeDiff / (60 * 60 * 24)), 'day');
 } else if (Math.abs(timeDiff) < 60 * 60 * 24 * 30) { // Within month
 return relativeTime.format(Math.round(timeDiff / ( 60 * 60 * 24 * 7)), 'week');
 } else if (Math.abs(timeDiff) < 60 * 60 * 24 * 365) { // Within year
 return relativeTime.format(Math.round(timeDiff / ( 60 * 60 * 24 * 30)), 'month');
 } else { // Year+
 return relativeTime.format(Math.round(timeDiff / (60 * 60 * 24 * 365)), 'year');
 }
 }
